questions.question: The system receives 100 million generation requests in a 30-day month and expects a 4x peak over the monthly average. About what peak request rate should capacity planning start from before headroom?
options: 15 images/s
39 images/s
154 images/s
400 images/s
questions.explanation: 100,000,000 / (30 x 24 x 60 x 60) is about 38.6 images/s. A 4x peak is about 154 images/s, before adding failure and deployment headroom.

questions.question: Which record most directly preserves the correctness of an inpainting request?
options: A mutable chat message containing the last prompt
An immutable generation specification containing the prompt, reference, mask, seed, controls, model version, and policy outcome
Only the final image URL because output inspection is sufficient
A shared cache key based on the requested style
questions.explanation: The immutable generation specification binds the requested edit boundary and all inputs to the exact model and policy decisions used to create the output.

questions.question: GPU capacity is saturated and the quality tier cannot meet the 25-second target. What is the safest product response?
options: Skip output inspection for jobs already rendered
Retry every job immediately until a worker becomes free
Offer an approved preview tier or an ETA for the final while keeping all release gates in force
Silently switch every request to a different model and remove its control settings
questions.explanation: Quality and wait time may degrade under pressure, but safety, rights, provenance, and requested edit semantics remain release constraints.

questions.question: Why must output policy run even after a prompt has passed input policy?
options: It lets the service avoid storing a job record
A model can create unsafe, policy-sensitive, or unexpected visual content from an apparently acceptable request
It guarantees that the user will prefer the image
It makes prompt policy unnecessary
questions.explanation: Input controls prevent clear violations and save compute, but generation is not perfectly predictable. Output inspection is an independent release gate.

questions.question: Which dependency failure should normally cause affected generated images to be held rather than delivered?
options: A product analytics consumer falls behind
The output safety and provenance service cannot complete its required checks
A thumbnail prefetch request times out
A noncritical dashboard aggregation is delayed
questions.explanation: The release invariant requires inspected, provenance-bearing output. Analytics and other asynchronous work can degrade independently, but the release gate cannot be bypassed.

questions.question: Which metric combination best detects a harmful change hidden by a better average aesthetic score?
options: Only total images generated and average GPU utilization
Prompt-alignment score, mask-boundary fidelity, output-policy recall, provenance coverage, and slice-level regression checks
The number of new model parameters and the image file size
The number of users who opened the generation screen
questions.explanation: A production release must evaluate request fidelity, safety, provenance, and subgroup behavior. A single aesthetic score cannot reveal failures in these independent constraints.
